The detected absorption line at 3.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV corresponds to a frequency of about 943 MHz and a wavelength of ~32 cm. This is the redshifted 21 cm hyperfine transition of neutral atomic hydrogen (HI), whose rest energy is 5.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV. The redshift z ≈ 0.51 matches the given distance of 2.1 Gpc.

In the Milky Way, the 21 cm line traces atomic hydrogen. While both warm and cold atomic phases contain HI, absorption lines—especially narrow ones—are predominantly produced by cold atomic clouds, which have lower spin temperatures and higher optical depths. Warm atomic gas is more easily observed in emission. Therefore, this absorption line is most likely associated with the cold atomic interstellar medium.

Answer: C
